doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Writing Fried Bananas lyrics and the New York dream
summary: She finishes a Fried Bananas lyric, tells of her husband's dare, and of her childhood longing for New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What a business. Speaking of writing lyrics, I’m going to read — this is an excerpt from an Anne Phillips lyric and you have to finish it. Okay? “But no matter how I have tried, this feeling inside —
[sings] How I have tried, this feeling inside, can’t be denied, so what if it’s done — it’s home. That’s “Fried Bananas.”

That’s right. You get to move on to the next round. You know when I read that about “Fried Bananas” I got out the Dexter Gordon thing and first of all I thought she’s going to have the term “fried bananas” in the lyrics because of the story that went with it. Then I listened to the whole thing and it’s quite clever and quite an accomplishment.
You did hear the whole story of my husband saying, “I’ve not seen you at the piano anymore?” © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
It was like a dare? He dared you to do it or something?

Yes. Yeah. And he literally opened up a new fake book and there was “Fried” he said, “Do that before I get home.” So I did. And the funny thing is I use the verse to it now. I’ve been doing — well on my birthday party I did this whole show and I started [sings] I was a kid/the night that I woke and cried/take me to New York City please/let’s ride to New York/That was my nirvana/No more little bitty/Gone to New York City/That’s all I could see/I dreamed it would be/The place that I would reside in/The place that I would call home. That that’s the beginning of my telling my story.
Yup. So it really is true, my mother did hear me crying and she ran up the stairs. I must have been about 14. And I said, “All my friends have been to New York and you only take me to Philadelphia.”
